name: Alpex Solar Ltd
tagline: North India's largest solar-module maker, backward-integrating into a 2.2GW TOPCon cell plant to capture the Jun-2026 DCR policy; growth is real but earnings are at a policy-window peak (Q1 FY27 PAT -6% on margin compression), leverage and finance costs are ramping fast, FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 116 Cr, and the cell plant has slipped to Sep-2026
business_overview: Alpex Solar -- North India's largest solar PV module manufacturer (Greater Noida), backward-integrating into TOPCon cell manufacturing (2.2GW G12R plant at Kosi Kotwan, Mathura) ahead of the mandated domestic-content (DCR) policy shift. Applied for ALMM List-II inclusion for the cell plant.
fundamentals_table: Rs 2,223 Cr; Q1 FY27 Rs 503 Cr (+32.4% YoY, -25% QoQ)
FY26 Rs 202 Cr (record); Q1 FY27 Rs 39.9 Cr (-5.7% YoY); net margin 7.9% vs 11.1%
Borrowings Rs 537 Cr (Mar 2026), D/E ~0.87x; Q1 FY27 finance cost Rs 15.0 Cr (+350% YoY); Rs 2,000 Cr borrowing authorisation sought via Jul-2026 postal ballot
FY24 -Rs 5 Cr, FY25 +Rs 69 Cr, FY26 -Rs 116 Cr (capex-driven cash burn)
65.90%, no pledge / no encumbrance declared FY26
fundamentals_narrative: Headline growth and returns remain exceptional (3yr sales CAGR ~125%, FY26 PAT Rs 202 Cr, ROE 52%), but the deep read shows the earnings are at a policy-window / cycle peak and are now compressing: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY yet PAT fell 5.7% as net margin dropped to 7.9% from 11.1%, finance costs jumped ~350% YoY to Rs 15 Cr, and depreciation and employee costs stepped up. FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 116 Cr as the 2.2GW cell capex absorbed cash, and the board has sought a Rs 2,000 Cr borrowing authorisation. Positives vs the prior pass: promoters declared no pledge/encumbrance for FY26, debtor days improved to 42 (from 63), and the DCR catalyst is confirmed and live with an ALMM List-II application filed. The 2.2GW TOPCon cell plant slipped from Aug to Sep 2026 (imported-machine problems plus a minor insured fire on 21-Jul-2026), and the community's environmental-clearance capacity dispute (1.6GW vs claimed 2.2GW) is still unresolved.
sentiment_summary: Read all 19 posts in the thread (2025-08 to 2026-08). Central catalyst: a Jun 2026 government policy requiring EPC players to use India-made modules with India-made cells (DCR), targeting the ~50GW of Indian module capacity that currently imports Chinese cells. Alpex is building a 2.2GW TOPCon cell facility to capture this. Management has consistently delivered on guided revenue-doubling since IPO.
community_signal: No trusted users in this thread, but the non-trusted debate is unusually well-informed and adversarial in a useful way: vikas_chandrawat (invested, 1.5yr holder) flagged receivables growing faster than revenue and rising interest costs as balance-sheet stress; a live, unresolved dispute (Aug 2026) over whether the new cell facility's environmental clearance covers 1.6GW or the company-claimed 2.2GW -- a real execution-credibility question.
bse_notes: 21-Jul-2026: minor fire at the Mathura cell factory, no injuries, insured, operations resumed. 19-Jul-2026: postal-ballot notice for director appointment, Rs 2,000 Cr borrowing authorisation, asset disposal and related-party transactions. Cell plant ALMM List-II application filed with MNRE.
bull_case: Specific, quantified DCR policy catalyst (Jun 2026) directly targets the exact gap Alpex is filling via backward integration into TOPCon cells; ALMM List-II application filed
Consistent execution track record -- management has delivered on guided revenue-doubling every year since IPO; 3yr sales CAGR ~125%
Cheap on headline (~12x trailing P/E, ~4.3x book) for a 40%+ ROCE / 50%+ ROE grower -- market is not pricing in a successful cell-integration margin uplift
Promoters carry no pledge/encumbrance (declared FY26); debtor days improved to 42 from 63
bear_case: Earnings are at a policy-window / cycle peak and already compressing: Q1 FY27 PAT -5.7% YoY, net margin 7.9% vs 11.1%, on a commoditising module business exposed to Chinese cell oversupply
Leverage ramping hard: borrowings Rs 537 Cr, D/E ~0.87x, finance costs +350% YoY, and a Rs 2,000 Cr further borrowing authorisation sought
FY26 operating cash flow -Rs 116 Cr -- growth is cash-consumptive and reported ROE overstates economic returns
Cell plant slipped again (Aug -> Sep 2026) on imported-machine issues + a July fire; EC-capacity dispute (1.6GW vs claimed 2.2GW) unresolved; no structural moat beyond policy protection
verdict_headline: A specific, well-timed DCR policy catalyst and un-ignorable growth at ~12x earnings, offset by peak-margin compression, a fast-ramping balance sheet, cash burn and a twice-slipped cell plant -- label kept via the growth exception, conviction capped at Medium
verdict_reasoning: The DCR policy catalyst and backward-integration strategy are specific and credible, and management's delivery track record is real (3yr sales CAGR ~125%).

four_box score is 2.5 (tam / moat / valuation all weak on commodity economics, thin moat and peak-cycle earnings), so thesis_fit '10x-in-2-3-years' is retained ONLY under the written exception -- un-ignorable growth (~125% 3yr sales CAGR) trading at ~12x trailing P/E -- which caps conviction at Medium with an execution-dependent caveat.

Conviction held at Medium: the FY26 pledge-clean confirmation and improved debtor days are offset by current, unresolved risks -- Q1 FY27 margin compression and negative FY26 operating cash flow, a finance-cost line up 350%, a Rs 2,000 Cr borrowing authorisation, a twice-delayed cell plant, and the unresolved EC-capacity dispute.
No formal red flag (no negative net worth, no SEBI action, no pledge); the concerns are execution and capital-intensity, not governance.
notes_short: DCR policy tailwind + 2.2GW cell backward integration at ~12x P/E, but Q1 FY27 margin compression, D/E ~0.87x with finance costs +350%, FY26 OCF -Rs 116 Cr, cell plant slipped to Sep-2026, EC-capacity dispute unresolved

four_box.note: tailwind yes -- Jun-2026 DCR policy + India solar-manufacturing push + ALMM is a real multi-year (policy-dependent) tailwind; tam weak -- large end-market but commodity module/cell economics and Chinese oversupply cap the profit headroom for a 10x off Rs 2,400 Cr; moat weak -- policy-protected capacity fill (ALMM/DCR), no structural cost or technology edge, TOPCon is table-stakes; valuation weak -- ~12x trailing P/E looks cheap but the earnings are at a policy/cycle peak already compressing and FCF is negative, so the low multiple is partly a cyclicality/leverage discount. Score 2.5 -> thesis_fit '10x-in-2-3-years' retained only via the written un-ignorable-growth exception in verdict_reasoning; conviction caps at Medium.
